The organising views are ready at **http://maker:4001** (please refresh). I've set up a few samples across the states so you can see them.

At the top there are now three tabs — **All**, **Read later**, and **Archive**. Let me guide you through each:

1. On **All**, find a bookmark and click **"☆ Read later"** on it. Then click the **Read later** tab — it should now appear there. (This is your separate reading list.)
2. Back on **All**, click **"Archive"** on a bookmark. Notice it disappears from All — then open the **Archive** tab to find it still safely kept, with a **"Restore to All"** option.
3. While on the **Read later** or **Archive** tab, try the search box or a tag chip — searching works *within* the current tab.

A few choices I made that I'd like your reaction to, since each could reasonably work another way:

- I set up **"Read later" as a toggle you can turn on or off at any time** from a saved bookmark (rather than a decision fixed when you first save it), and a small **"Read later" badge** shows on those items in the All list. Please check whether that matches how you think about a reading list.
- I set up **Archive so archived links leave All and Read later entirely** and live only in the Archive tab — still searchable there — keeping your main view uncluttered as you asked. Check that archived links disappearing from the main view (rather than just being greyed out) is what you want.

After trying all three: **do these organising behaviours match how you'd want to keep things tidy?**
